feastLines.line: 🔥 The fire settles. the woman in her 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm, the paramedic has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you — I put it down today." "It crouches low, tail lashing once, twice. The stripes go still. Then it comes." "A paw rises, claws out — casual, almost lazy. It is not lazy." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the person in their 60s, with grey-streaked hair says quietly "And you're still standing." the person in their 30s, with restless hands, the chimney sweep asks "Tell me you didn't g

🔥 The fire settles. Brayden has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A soft green glow under the water — I put it down today." "A soft green glow under the water. Pretty. That's the problem — it's pretty." "The whiskers go rigid — then lash." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Elif breathes "The fire feels smaller now." the person in their 30s, with restless hands, the chimney sweep says quietly "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Cameron has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Drum-Belly — I put it down today." "It rears up, belly swelling drum-taut, and beats it with both paws — BOOM. The air itself flinches." "It waddles left, then is suddenly right — a feint, testing whether your eyes or your ears are in charge." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Brayden mutters "The fire feels smaller now." Emma mutters "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Stan has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Flashbulb Moth — I put it down today." "It lands. It folds its wings. The light in the clearing changes, like someone adjusting a lamp." "It lets go of the air and simply... drifts. Somewhere else. Hard to predict." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Miguel mutters "The fire feels smaller now." Pavel asks "And you're still standing." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Cameron has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Seymour says quietly "Tell me you didn't go alone." Stan mutters "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Miguel has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "The Living Wire — I put it down today." "The water goes glass-still. A faint crackling, and the hairs on your arms lift." "The crackling fades. It slides backward into the black water, done spending itself — for now." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Brayden mutters "Tell me you didn't go alone." Emma asks "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Yasmin has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Choir Toad — I put it down today." "Its throat swells. The air goes thick. Every frog for a mile answers at once." "It crouches — clumsy, obvious, and faster than it looks." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Mara says "And you're still standing." Emma says "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Pavel has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Night Court — I put it down today." "No sound. That is the warning. The moon-shadow on the ground is growing — and there is no sound at all. Owls don't make sound when they hunt." "It missed — and it is already turning. The second dive re-aims at where you moved." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Miguel breathes "Say that again — slower." Seymour mutters "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Pavel has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Tick — I put it down today." "It waits. The questing legs wave — the tell." "Adjacent = attached. No dodge. It's ON you." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Mara says "Say that again — slower." Elif mutters "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

The beam follows your gaze. MOVE." "The reel stutters — outtakes. Embarrassing ones. Close up." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Pavel breathes "The fire feels smaller now." Nikos mutters "And you're still standing." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Pavel has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Speedbump — I put it down today." "It doesn't move. It hasn't moved in an hour. Its head is suddenly somewhere else." "It seals itself. The shell clicks shut — nearly invulnerable. Wait it out, or flip it." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Brayden asks "So it bleeds." Yasmin mutters "Tell me you didn't go alone." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Emma has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Static — I put it down today." "It finds your voice in the static. It WEARS it. 'Help— help me—' in YOUR voice. Moving won't help once it has you." "It drops the voice. No static, no words — it RUSHES, no telegraph at all. Back off." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Cameron mutters "So it bleeds." Stan says "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
The fire is built high. Nobody speaks while the count is taken — you can hear the wind past the edge of the light.
